caption:
Late RSVP wedding etiquette
What to say when a reply comes in late, when it names extra people, and when they turn up at the door anyway, with the exact texts to copy.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment:
Copy, paste, send:
1) Late, and there is room: “Thank you for telling us! We've added you, and we're so glad you can come.”
2) Late, after the caterer's date: “We wish we could, but our numbers are final. We'll miss you.”
3) Extra people on the reply (call to correct it): “Thanks for replying! Our invitation is for the two of you only. We can't wait to see you.” You can also cite venue size or budget.
4) Extra guests at the door: “So glad you're here. Let's find you a seat.” Then ask the caterer or planner to add seats and plates.
Norah is AI-generated.
comment_bait: Late yes or extra people: which would be harder for you to answer?

sources.fact: Wedding invitations are not negotiations; the inner envelope is the final word on who exactly is being invited. If a guest RSVPs with uninvited guests, call to correct it; couples can cite venue size or budget; if unlisted guests turn up, ask the caterer or planner to add seats and plates and welcome them rather than lecturing; late replies are up to the couple, but accommodate them when possible
sources.title: Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace

sources.fact: Venues and caterers typically need final headcounts one to two weeks before the wedding; the RSVP deadline sits at least ten days before that date so there is time to chase
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines
Inside Weddings: Handling Your Guests With Grace
